description: Write conditional CSS with media queries, breakpoints, min‑width, max‑width, and more.

slides.title: Syntax of a Media Query 📜
Breakpoints: Where the Layout Changes 🚧
slides.content:
# Choose Based on Content, Not Devices

Common breakpoints:
- Small: < 576px (phones)
- Medium: ≥ 576px (large phones / small tablets)
- Large: ≥ 768px (tablets)
- Extra large: ≥ 992px (desktop)
- XXL: ≥ 1200px (wide screens)

But don't tie them to specific devices; let your content guide you. When your design looks broken, add a breakpoint.

quizData.question: Which media query applies styles only when the viewport is 600px or wider?
quizData.explanation: `min-width: 600px` means the condition is true when width is 600px or more.

slides.title: Combining Conditions (AND / OR) ⛓️
Other Media Features 🖥️

quizData.question: A media query with `@media (min-width: 800px) and (max-width: 1200px)` applies when the screen width is between 800px and 1200px inclusive.
quizData.explanation: `min-width: 800px` requires width ≥ 800px, `max-width: 1200px` requires width ≤ 1200px. Together they cover that range.
